security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU's mstatus WARL write-mask (target/riscv/csr.c, typically in write_mstatus or a helper returning the legal writable bitmask) returns any of MIE, MPIE, SIE, SPIE, MPRV, MXR, SUM, TVM, TW, TSR as read-only zero when the corresponding privilege mode (S-mode, U-mode) or feature (page-based virtual memory via satp.MODE) IS implemented on the emulated hart. Conversely, the mask must return read-only zero when those modes/features are absent — over-approximating writability also leaks invalid state.
security_spec.summary: mstatus fields MIE/MPIE/SIE/SPIE/MPRV/MXR/SUM/TVM/TW/TSR must be writable when their dependent modes exist, else read-only 0 — QEMU WARL masking must dynamically track implemented privilege modes and satp.MODE writability

findings.finding: The WARL write-mask unconditionally includes SIE, SPIE, MPRV, SUM, MXR, TVM, TSR, TW regardless of whether S-mode (RVS), U-mode (RVU), or page-based virtual memory (satp.MODE != Bare) are implemented on the emulated hart. Per RISC-V privileged spec: SIE/SPIE must be read-only zero when S-mode is absent; MPRV must be read-only zero when U-mode is absent; SUM/MXR must be read-only zero when S-mode or paging is absent. The over-approximating mask allows guest software to write and subsequently read back WARL fields that hardware would force to zero, leaking false feature information and violating WARL constraints.
findings.snippet:
mask = MSTATUS_SIE | MSTATUS_SPIE | MSTATUS_MIE | MSTATUS_MPIE |
        MSTATUS_SPP | MSTATUS_MPRV | MSTATUS_SUM |
        MSTATUS_MPP | MSTATUS_MXR | MSTATUS_TVM | MSTATUS_TSR |
        MSTATUS_TW;

findings.finding: read_mstatus returns env->mstatus without applying any conditional read-as-zero masking for SIE, SPIE, MPRV, SUM, MXR, TVM, TSR, or TW. Combined with the over-approximating write mask, this means guest software can write 1 to SIE (etc.) on an M-mode-only hart and read the bit back as 1, directly contradicting the WARL spec that requires those bits to be read-only zero when their associated privilege modes/features are absent. This can confuse guest discovery probes (e.g., checking for S-mode support) and leaks internal emulator state.
TLB flush is correctly triggered on MXR transitions, which affect virtual memory interpretation.

MPP legalization correctly constrains writable values to only implemented privilege modes (M only when S/U absent; M,S when S present; M,S,U when U present). If new_mpp is invalid, the field is held unchanged — proper WARL behavior.

write_mstatush correctly applies mask only for implemented features: RVH gates MPV/GVA, Smdbltrp gates MDT. The MDT→MIE side-effect (clearing MIE when MDT is set to 1) is correct per the Smdbltrp extension spec.

write_sstatus delegates to write_mstatus after applying sstatus_v1_10_mask filtering — the sstatus filter is correct, but the underlying write_mstatus function still has the unconditional writability issue.
findings.snippet:
target_ulong newval = (env->mstatus & ~mask) | (val & mask);
    return write_mstatus(env, CSR_MSTATUS, newval, ra);

findings.finding: read_sstatus correctly masks env->mstatus through sstatus_v1_10_mask, which includes SSTATUS_SIE, SSTATUS_SPIE, SSTATUS_SUM, SSTATUS_MXR, etc. — only these S-mode-viewable bits are returned. This read path is correct.

Hypervisor register swapping correctly banks the S-level view of mstatus (MXR, SUM, SPP, SPIE, SIE, UXL, VS, FS, SPELP, SDT) into vsstatus/mstatus_hs and restores the corresponding bank on context switch. No security concern.
